blocks.text: An economy is organised into **three sectors — primary (agriculture), secondary (industry) and tertiary (services)**. India has shifted to a **services-led economy**, though **agriculture still employs the largest share of workers** — a structural feature central to economic geography.

rows: Farming, livestock, fishing, forestry, mining; **~45% of employment but ~18% of GDP**; India a top producer of milk, pulses, spices, rice, wheat.
Manufacturing, construction, power; ~**25-27% of GDP**; 'Make in India'.
Trade, IT, finance, transport, tourism; **largest share ~53% of GDP**; India's growth engine (IT/ITeS).
Services led (skipping a big industrial phase); agriculture's GDP share falling but employment share high.

items: Services = largest GDP share (~53%); agriculture = largest employment but ~18% GDP.
India's unusual services-led (not industry-led) transition is the key structural point.

prelimsPointers: Three sectors — **primary (agriculture), secondary (industry), tertiary (services)**.
**Services** contribute the **largest share of GDP (~53%)**.
**Agriculture** employs ~**45%** of workers but only ~**18%** of GDP.
India is a **top global producer of milk, pulses, jute, spices; 2nd in rice, wheat, sugarcane**.
**IT/ITeS** and software services drive tertiary-sector exports.
India's transition is **services-led**, atypically bypassing a large manufacturing phase.
**Quaternary/Quinary** (knowledge/decision) sectors are sometimes added.
mainsAngles: Analyse the sectoral composition of the Indian economy and its structural shift.

glossary.definition: The extractive sector — agriculture, mining, fishing, forestry.
The services sector (trade, IT, finance), India's largest by GDP share.
The changing relative weights of sectors as an economy develops.

sections.heading: Basic industries — agro, mineral, forest, fuel & manpower-based

blocks.text: Industries are classified by their **raw-material/resource base** — **agro-based, mineral-based, forest-based, fuel-based and manpower/knowledge-based**. Their **location** follows the availability of these inputs, giving each region a distinctive industrial character (including **Andhra Pradesh**).

rows: **Textiles (cotton, jute), sugar, food processing, edible oils, seafood** — near farm inputs.
**Iron & steel (TISCO, SAIL, RINL-Vizag), cement (limestone), aluminium** — near ores/coal.
**IT, pharma, electronics** — near skilled labour (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Vizag).

items: Classify by resource base (agro/mineral/forest/fuel/manpower) with examples; location follows inputs.
AP: RINL Vizag Steel (mineral), HPCL refinery (fuel), pharma (manpower).

prelimsPointers: Industries classified by base — **agro, mineral, forest, fuel, manpower/knowledge**.
**Agro-based** — cotton/jute textiles, sugar, food & seafood processing.
**Mineral-based** — **iron & steel (TISCO Jamshedpur — first; SAIL; RINL-Visakhapatnam), cement, aluminium**.
**Iron & steel** is a **basic/heavy industry** — the backbone of industrialisation.
**Forest-based** — paper (Rajahmundry in AP), plywood; **fuel-based** — refineries (HPCL Vizag).
**Manpower/knowledge** — IT (Bengaluru, Hyderabad), pharma (a major AP strength).
Industrial **location** depends on raw materials, power, labour, market & transport (Weber's theory).
mainsAngles: Classify industries by their resource base and discuss their location factors.

glossary.definition: A heavy industry (like iron and steel) that supplies raw materials to other industries.
Manufacturing that uses agricultural raw materials, e.g. textiles and sugar.
An industry (e.g. IT) not tied to raw-material location, sited by skilled manpower.

blocks.text: **Transport and trade** integrate the economy and connect India to the world. India has a vast **road, rail, water and air network** and a growing **foreign trade**, though it runs a persistent **trade deficit** — with **Andhra Pradesh's ports** a key export gateway.

rows: India has the **2nd-largest road network** in the world; **National Highways** carry most freight; NH-44 longest.
**13 major ports**; Mumbai/JNPT largest; **Visakhapatnam** largest on east coast; inland waterways.
**Persistent trade deficit** (imports > exports); top imports **crude oil, gold, electronics**; exports **petroleum products, gems, pharma, textiles**.

items: Roads carry most freight; railways = largest employer; 13 major ports (Vizag largest on east coast).
India runs a trade deficit (crude oil & gold top imports); AP ports = export gateway.

prelimsPointers: India has the **world's 2nd-largest road network**; **NH-44** is the longest national highway.
**Indian Railways** — India's **largest employer**; 4th-largest rail network globally.
**Golden Quadrilateral** connects **Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata** (roads).
India has **13 major ports**; **Visakhapatnam** — largest cargo port on the **east coast**; JNPT (Mumbai) — largest container port.
**AP** has ~**975 km coastline** (2nd longest) with ports at **Vizag, Gangavaram, Krishnapatnam, Kakinada**.
India runs a **persistent trade deficit**; top imports — **crude oil, gold, electronics**.
Major exports — **refined petroleum, gems & jewellery, pharmaceuticals, textiles, engineering goods**.
mainsAngles: Assess India's transport network and foreign-trade pattern, with reference to Andhra's ports.

glossary.definition: The highway network linking Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.
A centrally-administered port of national importance; India has 13, including Visakhapatnam.
The excess of a country's imports over its exports.
